text:
Situation: Corvale Lakeside holds 15 units of polyethylene glycol 3350 and electrolytes with orange flavor (236 g/4 L), providing 8.9 days of supply at current use. Corvale General holds 271 units (27.7 days) and Corvale East holds 182 units (24.9 days). The product is not on FDA’s drug shortage list as of 2026-10-21.

Why (FDA record): The labeler and registered plant for NDC 64380076721 is Strides Pharma Science Limited. FDA’s most recent inspection of that plant ended on 2026-05-20 and was classified VAI.

Our position: No national shortage exists. The issue is localized maldistribution. Corvale Lakeside is below the two‑week target; Corvale General and Corvale East each have more than two weeks and can spare stock.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 9 units (4 L each) from Corvale General to Corvale Lakeside. This raises Lakeside to approximately 14 days of supply while General retains over two weeks. Approval required: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
2. If General cannot release units, transfer 9 units (4 L each) from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside. East retains over two weeks. Approval required: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).

Not recommended: Purchasing additional units from the manufacturer or secondary distributors while internal stock is adequate. No clinical protocol changes are proposed; those are for the treating clinicians and the committee.
